## D9: the C1 rule is asymmetric and under-specified

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The C1 rule will probably return UNDETERMINED, and it is asymmetric. If R-72's proviso was unmet but no blocking text covers RED, the rule says UNDETERMINED. By R-72's own logic the conditional authorization never became operative, so the result should be NON-CONFORMS by default. No default reading of 'WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED' is fixed for the likely case where no scoping text exists. Entry-into-force times for R-77 to R-80 are to come 'from adoption records', but these rulings may not be status-mediated at all, and no fallback is given. The MD and the JSON also scope the 'and' in the CONFORMS branch differently."

**(2) Correction.** (§2)
- **Default state:** WP-4B work is UNAUTHORIZED at 16:10 unless R-72's proviso is *shown* met, by texts in force before 16:10.
- **Default scope:** "WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED" covers all WP-4B work, including producer-agnostic RED test code, unless a text in force before 16:10 explicitly narrows it.
- **Fallback for rulings that are not status-mediated:** entry into force is not earlier than the ruling's recording time, graded by §0.9. A stated date is SOURCE_STATED.
- **One structure** for CONFORMS: **P ∧ ¬B**. The MD version is kept, because R-72's authorization and R-77's block are separate conditions, and both must be satisfied.
- **UNDETERMINED** is reserved for two cases:
  - required texts cannot be obtained;
  - the time at which a relevant text entered force, relative to 16:10, is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
- If the texts are obtained and do not show the proviso met, the result is NON-CONFORMS by default.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- **Asymmetry removed.** The default follows R-72's own conditional form: an authorization that is conditional on a proviso is operative only if the proviso holds. So the case "proviso unmet, no covering block" now yields NON-CONFORMS.
- **Default scope fixed.** The case with no scoping text now has a determinate reading.
- **Fallback added.** Rulings without an adoption record now have a time premise.
- **Consistency.** A single boolean structure makes the MD and the JSON identical.
- **Guard against unseen evidence.** UNDETERMINED remains only where a premise is actually unobservable. So the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen: missing texts give UNDETERMINED, not NON-CONFORMS.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **C1 / P2:** the likely verdict moves from UNDETERMINED to NON-CONFORMS, if R-73..R-76 are obtained and do not show the proviso met.
- **C1 bearing:** changes as in D6. It no longer requires that nothing responded before R-87.
- **G-D1 applies.** If the absence of a permitting text before 16:10 relies on R-81..R-85 having had no force until R-86 adopted them, the result is DISJUNCTIVE {H-D status clause, H-B conformance}.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D9.**
> - **P** = R-72's RED condition and proviso ("no unresolved governance blockers"; the named ARB decisions and scope ruling have landed) are shown met by texts in force before 16:10.
> - **B** = a text in force before 16:10 blocks WP-4B, read by default as covering all WP-4B work including producer-agnostic RED, and no text in force before 16:10 narrows that scope to exclude RED.
>
> Verdicts:
> - **CONFORMS** iff P ∧ ¬B.
> - **NON-CONFORMS** iff the required texts (R-72 to R-80) were obtained and ¬(P ∧ ¬B).
> - **UNDETERMINED** iff a required text could not be obtained, or the entry-into-force time of a text that decides P or B is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE relative to 16:10.
>
> Entry into force: an adoption form, if the ruling is status-mediated; otherwise, not earlier than its recording time. Stated dates are SOURCE_STATED.
>
> The 16:10 time of R11 is itself a git date (SOURCE_STATED). The verdict carries that label.

---

## D10: the P1 census and the P8 tendency are under-specified

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The P1-HB census refutes only **H-B restricted to window W**, and the spec does not say so. Reading H-B's clause as existential is also an interpretive choice that is not labelled UNKNOWN. Under the other reading ('when the work condition is met, the state changes'), one clean counter-instance would be enough. The P8 'tendency ⇒ census' option gives no threshold, so it cannot be tested."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P1-HB:** label the quantifier reading UNKNOWN, and test both readings:
  - **Reading 1a (existential):** the census over W. A negative result is stated as "H-B reading 1a is not instantiated in W". It is never stated as "H-B refuted".
  - **Reading 1b (conditional-universal):** one eligible target whose work condition is met, and whose state is unchanged by NIF until a separate act, refutes 1b.
- **P8:** drop the tendency reading. No source gives a threshold, and inventing one would be arbitrary. P8 is tested as a universal. If H-B's authors intend a tendency, P8 is declared NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED and is not scored.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The logical force of each test now matches its quantifier:
  - An existential claim is refuted only by exhausting its domain, so the conclusion is limited to the exhausted domain W.
  - A conditional-universal claim is refuted by one instance.
- Reporting both readings keeps the interpretation from being decided after the fact.
- Dropping the tendency reading removes the only untestable option. Keeping it without a threshold would have left P8 unfalsifiable.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P1-HB:** the conclusion is scoped to W, and a second, stronger test (1b) is added.
- **P8-HB:** only the universal reading remains.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D10.** P1-HB is scored under both readings.
> - 1a: "not instantiated in W" or "instantiated".
> - 1b: FIRED if at least one eligible counter-instance is found (with NIF).
>
> Neither result is generalized beyond W. P8 is universal only. The tendency reading is NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED.

---

## D11: attestation fields assume artefacts that no input establishes

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The feasibility section is hedged, but the **attestation fields assume** artefacts that no input establishes: CI runs with CI start times; 'server push time' (git history does not record it); 'adopted' R-86 and R-90 (R-90 appears in the inputs in a withdrawal context); adoption records for R-77, R-79 and R-80; 'DA session logs'; version control of IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md; a register kept as a git file. STATE lists only a register, a few session logs and **one** commit."

**(2) Correction.**
- Phrase every such field as "if such an artefact exists".
- Give a fallback for each, with its grade, in the table in §0.11.
- Mark R-90's status as UNKNOWN.
- Note that git dates (including R11's 16:10) are client-set (§0.9).

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The defect is an existence assumption hidden inside field definitions.
- After the correction, every field is defined whether or not its preferred artefact exists: either the fallback applies with a stated grade, or the field is UNDETERMINED.
- So no result can depend silently on an artefact that no input shows exists.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No. Some outcomes are downgraded, for example to FIRED-CONDITIONAL or UNDETERMINED, when the preferred artefacts do not exist.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D11.** Every attestation names a preferred artefact "if it exists", a fallback, and the grade of the fallback (§0.11). A field whose preferred and fallback sources are both missing is UNDETERMINED. The capture reports which artefacts exist.

---

## D12: P7-HD depends on motive; P8-HD repeats P1

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "P7's H-D falsifier ('treated as authorized **because** the predecessor was accepted') depends on motive and cannot be observed as behaviour. It also cannot fire in the R-89 episode, because an authorizing act (R-89) exists. P8's H-D falsifier just repeats P1."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P7-HD:** NOT_APPLICABLE to the R-89 episode.
- **P7-HD in other episodes:** restated in behavioural and NIF terms. NIF shows the successor authorized and in force, and no norm-making act in a complete DCS produced that authorization. This *is* P1 on the gate, and it is scored under P1 only.
- **P8-HD:** points to P1 and is not scored separately.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The motive clause ("because") is removed, so every remaining condition is observable.
- In the R-89 episode, the premise "no authorizing act" is false by construction, since R-89 exists as a text. So declaring the limb NOT_APPLICABLE is exact.
- Scoring P7-HD and P8-HD under P1 only removes the double counting.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P7-HD:** it is dropped for the R-89 episode, and elsewhere merged into P1.
- **P8-HD:** it is merged into P1.
- H-D's operational predictions are therefore tested only through P1, P4 and P5.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D12.** P7-HD is NOT_APPLICABLE when any norm-making act authorizing the successor exists in the DCS, whatever that act's status. Otherwise, P7-HD and P8-HD are instances of P1-HD and are scored only there.

---

## D13: the status-mediation upgrade is only partial

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "Item 1 (an adoption entry written by the adopter) is still the norm-maker's own act; only its system time and authenticated identity are independent. The behavioural contrast (item 3) is empty unless work was ready and waiting during the prepared interval. As written, the upgrade moves status mediation only **part of the way** to independent observation."

**(2) Correction.** (§3)
- **Item 1:** relabelled as the norm-maker's own act. Only its recording time and its AUTH_ID are independent (FR-D7).
- **New item 0:** NIF-A for status, if Part C finds such a channel.
- **Item 2:** uptake is restricted to NIF-B (third-party application). NIF-C is recorded only.
- **Item 3:** the contrast gets an **eligibility condition**. During the prepared interval, a work item that depends on the ruling was *pending*: its preconditions were met, and it was queued or planned, attested by an artefact with a system-recorded time. A contrast without such an item is VACUOUS and is not scored.
- **Absence of work** in the prepared interval requires a complete execution channel (FR-D5e).

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The upgrade was partial on two counts:
  - Its first item was not independent. The correction now claims only what is independent (time and identity), and it adds the only fully independent source (NIF-A).
  - Its contrast could be vacuous. The eligibility condition ensures that "no execution during the prepared interval" is informative: work was ready, so its absence is a behavioural difference and not a lack of opportunity.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, for H-D's status clause (P4). An observed contrast now counts only if it is eligible. H-B's predictions are not affected, because H-B is silent here (SOURCE FACT: IDENTIFIABILITY P4).

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D13.** Status mediation counts as independently observed only if:
> - (0) NIF-A records the status transition, **or**
> - (1) an adoption form has a recording time and AUTH_ID, **and** (2) NIF-B uptake follows adoption, **and** (3) an **eligible** contrast is present: pending dependent work existed during the prepared interval, and a complete execution channel shows no execution on it and no NIF-B application before adoption.
>
> Otherwise, status mediation stays SELF_REPORTED or PARTIALLY_INDEPENDENT.

---

## D14: labels and optional items

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The ranking is labelled INFERENCE but is a judgement (PROPOSAL). The R-86 'waiting' quote is a SOURCE FACT; reading it as a behavioural instance is INFERENCE. P4 lists R-88's text, which only orders the rulings and says nothing about force. P7's GREEN/VERIFY CI run serves C2's evidence limb, not the gate falsifier. The 'input conflict' may be only apparent: '§WP-4 remains OPEN' may refer to WP-4 as a whole, not WP-4B, and C2's textual order does not establish the order of entry into force."

**(2) Correction.**
- **Ranking:** relabelled PROPOSAL.
- **R-86 "waiting":** the quote is SOURCE FACT; reading it as a behavioural instance is INFERENCE.
- **R-88 text:** OPTIONAL.
- **GREEN/VERIFY run:** OPTIONAL, and serves C2's evidence limb only.
- **Input conflict:** restated as "possibly only apparent", for two reasons. "§WP-4 remains OPEN" may refer to WP-4 as a whole. And C2 orders texts, which is SOURCE_STATED_ORDER of drafting, not an order of entry into force.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.** Each item is a mislabel or a wrongly required field. Relabelling or marking a field OPTIONAL fixes each one completely, and none of them is a premise of a falsifier.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D14.** Judgements are labelled PROPOSAL. Readings of quotes are labelled INFERENCE. Fields that are not premises of any falsifier are marked OPTIONAL. Textual order is labelled SOURCE_STATED_ORDER, and it never establishes the order of entry into force.

# PART A (continued). The complete corrected specification 1bb-r1

## §0. Scope and shared rules

### §0.1 Scope [UNCHANGED]
- **SOURCE FACT:** No prediction is identified on the current corpus (IDENTIFIABILITY `identified: []`).
- **PROPOSAL:** A prediction is in scope if some observation puts one hypothesis at risk while the other survives it. In scope: **P1** (only under H-B reading 1), **P2, P4, P5, P7, P8**. Excluded:
  - **P3**: act-mediated feedback fits both hypotheses, and its act-less part is P1.
  - **P6**: both hypotheses are met at every record boundary.
- **[NEW D1]** Being in scope is necessary but not sufficient. Each prediction's discrimination status also depends on NIF availability (§1.7).

### §0.2 Labels [UNCHANGED, extended]
- SOURCE FACT, INFERENCE, PROPOSAL and UNKNOWN, as in 1bb.
- **[NEW D1, D5, D11]** Grades, order labels and categories are defined in §0.3, §0.4 and §0.9.

### §0.3 The six distinctions [NEW D1; HUMAN-DECISIONS]
These categories are recorded separately for every episode. None is inferred from another, except by the rules stated here.

| Code | Distinction | What can establish it | What can never establish it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N-EXISTS** | The norm exists: a text of the norm is recorded (including PREPARED texts). | The record's text. Its time is a recording time (§0.9). | — |
| **N-FORCE** | The norm is in force at t. | NIF-A, or NIF-B (labelled N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL]). The graded fallback (§0.4) gives at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL. | The ruling's self-assertion; statements by the maker; recording time; executor behaviour; N-EXISTS alone. |
| **N-KNOWN** | The norm is known, or claimed, to be in force by actor X. | X's statement: NIF-C if X is a third party; MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION if X is the maker; SELF_ASSERTION if the statement is inside the ruling. | It never establishes N-FORCE. |
| **ACT-CONF** | An act according to the norm: an execution at t whose operation is permitted by the norms in force at t⁻. | An execution trace plus N-FORCE of a permitting norm at t⁻. | An execution trace alone. |
| **ACT-CONTRA** | An act contrary to the norm: an execution at t whose operation is not permitted at t⁻. | An execution trace plus N-FORCE of a prohibiting norm at t⁻, or the absence of any permitting norm in force at t⁻ (which requires a complete DCS, §0.8). | An execution trace alone. |
| **N-CHANGE-NOACT** | The norm changes without a norm-making act. | N-FORCE at t1 ≠ N-FORCE at t2, both by NIF; plus a complete DCS showing no norm-making act in [t1,t2], no prior conditional act producing the change, and no late-recorded act claiming effect in [t1,t2]. | A work event alone (HUMAN-DECISIONS). A ruling asserting its own adoption. |

### §0.4 Independent observables of the norm in force (NIF) and rule G-D1 [NEW D1]
- **NIF-A (independent norm-status record).** An entry in a channel that meets independence criteria I1–I4 (Part C §C.4) and records the *normative state* of the norm (in force or not in force) at t, with a system-generated time. Its availability is determined by Part C.
- **NIF-B (third-party application).** An act by an actor who is not the maker or adopter of the norm and not the executor of the work under test. The act applies the norm as binding: it grants, refuses, accepts or blocks on the norm's basis. It must carry AUTH_ID and a recording time.
  - It establishes N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL]. This is a PROPOSAL: application produces normative consequences, which are observable effects of force; citation does not.
  - If the application is later expressly voided as erroneous, its grade drops to FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
- **NIF-C (third-party citation).** A statement by such an actor that the norm governs, without applying it. It establishes N-KNOWN only. It is recorded, and it never fires a falsifier.
- **Not NIF:**
  - the executor's work under the norm (ACT);
  - the ruling's self-assertion ("effective immediately");
  - statements by the maker or adopter ("R-89 already governs authorization");
  - register recording times.
- **Graded fallback (maker's records).** This fallback is allowed only where §1.7 permits it. A premise about force may be taken from the norm-maker's records (text, adoption forms, recording times) in a DCS shown complete (§0.8). A falsifier built on such a premise is at most **FIRED-CONDITIONAL**, with the condition "the maker's records state force accurately".
- **G-D1.** If a premise "N (not) in force at t" is established only by (a) executor behaviour or (b) applying H-D's status rule (force only through adoption) to the maker's records, then every falsifier that uses it is graded **DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, H-B clause}**. This means "at least one fails; which one is not identified".

### §0.5 Attestation rule [CHANGED D7]
1B's three conditions are kept, and their scope is corrected.
- **Observation versus attestation.** A record R of an act is the observation of that act. R may attest only two things about itself:
  - its writer identity, graded AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID;
  - its recording time, graded by §0.9.

  R never attests its stated effective date or the norm's force.
- A field of any other observation is **independently attested** only if its attesting artefact:
  1. has a writer different from the maker, the adopter and the executor **[UNCHANGED in substance]**;
  2. does not copy the ruling's self-statements. Artefacts that *cite* the ruling are admissible as *observations* of uptake (NIF-B, NIF-C, ACT) **[CHANGED D7]**;
  3. carries a system-generated timestamp. A committer or author date is client-set, and is SOURCE_STATED (§0.9) **[CHANGED D11]**.
- Anything a ruling says about itself is self-report: "effective immediately", "R-89 already governs" **[UNCHANGED]**.
- **SOURCE FACT:** recording time ≠ decision time ≠ entry into force **[UNCHANGED]**. **[CHANGED D5, D9]** Entry into force comes from an adoption form (AF-1 to AF-3) when the ruling is status-mediated. Otherwise it is "not earlier than its recording time". It never comes from the time a row was recorded, taken as a decision time.

### §0.6 Declared channel set and capability register [CHANGED D5]
- **Capability register v0** **[CHANGED D5(f)]**. This is frozen before acquisition, not before reading: R-86 and R-90 have been read through the inputs.
  - **SOURCE FACT:** R-86 names the Decision Authority (DA) as the only adopter.
  - **SOURCE FACT (STATE):** Chief-prepared rulings gain force when the DA adopts them.
  - **UNKNOWN:** who is capable of making operational dispositions (R-94 type). The operational/constitutional split is known only through IDENTIFIABILITY's reading of R-90, which appears in a withdrawal context. It is resolved only by R-90's text and status in Stage 1. If it remains unresolved, P5 is NON-DISCRIMINATING.
- **Declared channel set (DCS) for norm-making acts, v0** **[CHANGED D5(a)]**:
  - **K-REG**: the register of rulings, and its write history if it is versioned.
  - **K-SESS**: session logs (S0804, S0815, and later ones).
  - **K-PROG**: IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md, which holds Chief dispositions and execution reports.

  DCS v1 = DCS v0 plus any channel for which Part C returns Q1 = YES and Q2 ∋ {ADOPTION_EVENT, APPROVAL_EVENT, NORM_STATE}. DCS v1 is closed before Stage 1.
- **"No act"** means "no norm-making act in DCS v1 in the window, with DCS v1 shown complete (§0.8)". It never means proving that no unrecorded act happened anywhere **[UNCHANGED in intent]**.
- **OUT_OF_CHANNEL_ACT** **[NEW D5(a)]**: a norm-making act found outside DCS v1. It shows that DCS v1 is incomplete for that target, and it makes the "no act" premise UNDETERMINED. It is never scored as N-CHANGE-NOACT.
- **Late recording** **[NEW D5(b)]**: see §0.9.
- **Adoption forms** **[NEW D5(c)]**. This list is exhaustive.
  - **AF-1**: the status annotation of the ruling row changes to ADOPTED (or "adopted"), written under the DA's identity.
  - **AF-2**: a separate entry by the DA that names the ruling id or ids and contains an adoption performative ("adopt", "adopted", "hereby adopts").
  - **AF-3**: a DA ruling that declares named prepared rulings governing, in performative form. This is the R-86 pattern: "These become governing rulings effective immediately".
  - **Not an adoption:** a descriptive assertion by the maker that force already exists, such as "R-89 already governs authorization". This is MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION.
  - **Sensitivity:** the outcome under the opposite classification is reported, but never scored.
- **Identity** **[NEW D5(d)]**:
  - **AUTH_ID**: a signature verified against a key list fixed before Stage 1, or an account-bound record on the hosting server (an approval, merge or audit event).
  - **ACTOR_SET_ID**: git author or committer fields, and names in text.

  If an identity-dependent premise has only ACTOR_SET_ID, the grade is at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL.

### §0.7 Execution-channel register [NEW D5(e)]
- **Execution channel EC v0:**
  - the git repository or repositories named by the human before Part B runs (Part B §1);
  - CI run records, if Part C finds that they exist.
- An **execution trace** is defined in Part B §3.
- An **absence of work** on target X is admissible only if EC is shown complete for X (§0.8). Otherwise it is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE.

### §0.8 Absence and completeness [NEW D2, D5]
An absence claim ("no act", "no adoption", "no waiver", "no work", "no response") counts as a falsifier premise only if the channel is shown complete over the window. That requires all four of the following:
1. **Coverage:** the channel is *required* for that kind of event, by a rule in force over the window, shown by NIF-A or by configuration enforced by the host (Part C Q6).
2. **Capture:** the capture is not shallow or partial, and its refs equal the server's refs at capture time.
3. **Retention:** records covering the window are retained.
4. **Integrity:** there is no undetected deletion or rewrite in the window, shown by an audit log or by tamper-evidence.

Otherwise the absence is **NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE**, and a falsifier that needs it is **UNDETERMINED**.

45	
46	### New defects introduced or left visible by the repair
47	
48	| # | Class | Where | Defect | Consequence / fix |
49	|---|---|---|---|---|
50	| **N1** | formal reasoning; independence | §0.4 NIF-B; §0.3 N-FORCE row; O3; FR-D13(2) | **NIF-B is behavioural, so the D1 confound returns one actor further out.** A third party "applying R-89 as binding" while R-89 is not adopted is explained by H-D (the third party acted contrary to the unchanged norm, or erred) and by H-B (practice changed the norm). This is exactly the REVIEW-1bb D1 argument, applied to a non-executor. The spec treats it as N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL], and O3 scores **P4-HD FIRED**. This collapses distinction 4 (the third party's act according to a norm) into distinction 2 (the norm in force). Downgrading only when the application is "expressly voided" makes silence count as force. | Extend G-D1 from "executor behaviour" to "any behaviour". If a force premise rests only on NIF-B, grade it DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, third-party conformance}. Only NIF-A (or NIF-B together with NIF-A) can give FIRED. |
51	| **N2** | formal reasoning; substantive | §0.3 ACT-CONTRA ("absence of any permitting norm … requires a complete DCS"); graded fallback; FR-D9 default "unauthorized unless P shown"; O5 "baseline of no authorization" | **G-D1 is too narrow.** It catches premises that use H-D's *status* rule (force only via adoption). It does not catch premises that use H-D's *act-exclusivity* clause (P1: norms change only through acts). The inference "no permitting act in a complete DCS ⇒ no permitting norm in force" is valid only if H-D's P1 clause holds. Under H-B reading 1, a permission can arise from work without an act. So P2, C1 and O5 falsify H-B conformance on a premise that presupposes H-D. | Add a G-D1(c) rule: a non-permission premise derived from the absence of a permitting act grades DISJUNCTIVE {H-D P1 clause, H-B conformance}, unless NIF-A shows the state. |
52	| **N3** | formal reasoning | §1.7 P2, P5-HB and P7 rows vs the P4 row; §0.6 MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION | **Asymmetric evidential standard.** The maker's records are admitted as a graded fallback (FIRED-CONDITIONAL, "maker's records state force accurately") when they cut against H-B. The maker's record that states force ("R-89 already governs") is barred even as a conditional premise when it cuts against H-D. The TASK requires NIF *or* NON-DISCRIMINATING. The fallback is neither, and it is offered to one side only. | Either allow the fallback symmetrically (P4-HD FIRED-CONDITIONAL on MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION) or on neither side. Otherwise declare P2 and P7 NON-DISCRIMINATING or FIRED-CONDITIONAL without NIF, and state that the condition includes H-D P1 (N2). |
53	| **N4** | source interpretation | §0.6 AF list; D5(4) | "R-89 already governs", written by the **sole adopter**, is frozen as not an adoption, and the sensitivity result is "never scored". Together with N1 this gives a concrete false falsification of H-D: the DA declares R-89 governing, a third party applies it, and O3 fires P4-HD, although under H-D the DA's declaration is plausibly the adoption. | Label the classification PROPOSAL/UNKNOWN. Score O3 only if it holds under **both** classifications. Otherwise grade it FIRED-CONDITIONAL(AF-reading). |
54	| **N5** | formal reasoning; M-TIME | FR-D9 entry-into-force fallback; §0.5 | "Entry into force not earlier than recording time" is (a) not implied by the inputs: decision and effect can precede recording, which the spec's own late-recording rule concedes. It is also (b) only a *lower* bound. So "text in force before 16:10" can never be shown through the fallback. P is then unshowable and NON-CONFORMS follows by default. At the same moment "entry into force NOT_IDENTIFIABLE relative to 16:10" is true, so NON-CONFORMS and UNDETERMINED both hold, and the verdict is not a function. | Give the verdicts a precedence (UNDETERMINED first). Use the fallback only as an existence bound. Where no upper bound on entry into force exists, P and B are NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, which gives UNDETERMINED. |
55	| **N6** | formal reasoning; evidence scope | FR-D9 P ("no unresolved governance blockers") | Showing P requires showing an **absence**. By §0.8 that needs a complete channel, which is practically unattainable (SC-4). So failing to show an absence becomes NON-CONFORMS, and an H-B falsifier fires on NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE. This contradicts §0.8, FR-D5(e) and D9's own sufficiency claim ("the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen"). | If the proviso's absence clause is NOT-EVIDENCED, C1 is UNDETERMINED, not NON-CONFORMS. |
56	| **N7** | formal reasoning | §5 outcome table | **Not exhaustive and not exclusive.** (i) Trace cites R-89, ACC, ¬AD, no NIF: no row. (ii) ¬G (gate not in force): no row. (iii) MENTION_ONLY and CAPTURE_ERROR (B.9 labels) are not mapped. (iv) **O5 lacks ¬ACC.** If WP-4B's acceptance is in force, the R-72 gate is satisfied and the work is authorized, yet O5 scores "P7-HB/P2-type FIRED". (v) The joint firing of O2 and O3, and the precedence of O6 over the other rows, are unstated. | Rebuild the table as a decision procedure over (trace class, ACC, G, WV, AD, F89 source), evaluated in a fixed order. Add ¬ACC to O5. |
57	| **N8** | formal reasoning; evidence scope | FR-D2; O0; Stage 1 gate | After D1, P4-HD (O3) is "whatever the work was", so it does not need a WP-4C-1 trace. Yet O0 says "P4 … discriminate nothing", and S1-e and S1-f (the only NIF acquisitions for R-89) run only if a trace exists. P4 is dropped for a reason that no longer applies. | Run S1-a, S1-b, S1-e and S1-f for P4 regardless of O0. Only P7 is gated on a trace. |
58	| **N9** | evidence scope | FR-D5(b); S1-b | The late-recording rule cannot fire: S1-b reads the DCS "over the P7 window" only, so acts recorded after the window are never acquired. Acts decided in W but recorded later *without* stating an effect date are not covered at all. | Extend S1-b to the full DCS history up to capture. Treat any post-window act on the same target as possibly late (NOT_IDENTIFIABLE), whether or not it states a date. |
59	| **N10** | evidence scope | S1-b; P7 WV | "No waiver in force at t_w⁻" needs waivers recorded *before* the window start, but S1-b is bounded by the window. | Read the waiver history from the root of the record. |
60	| **N11** | evidence scope | D6 vs §5 | "Stage 1 checks whether R-91 or R-94 refer to R11" appears in no S1 item, and Stage 1 is gated on a WP-4C-1 trace. | Add it as a P8 item, not gated on the trace. |
61	| **N12** | coding | FR-D8 P1 eligibility | The per-clause satisfaction rule is "written before Stage 1", so it is not frozen now. The eligibility definition also derives H-B's "work condition" from the text of H-D-style conditional acts. | Freeze the rules now, or mark P1 NOT_FROZEN. |
62	| **N13** | wording | §0.9 grades; §0.3 N-KNOWN; §0.6 vs C.5 | The grade vocabulary omits NON-DISCRIMINATING, LEGITIMATED, VACUOUS, ONE-SIDED and NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED, which are all used. N-KNOWN is defined as "known, **or claimed**", which merges factive knowledge (distinction 3) with assertion. DCS v1 membership includes NORM_STATE in §0.6 and the JSON, but not in the C.5 consequences. | Harmonise. |
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 2. D1 assessment
67	
68	- **Is a NIF specified per prediction?** Yes. §1.7 and `nif_matrix` give each limb a requirement and a "without it" status. This part of TASK is met in form.
69	- **Does the spec avoid presenting a dual-explainable observation as a discriminator?** Not fully. Two dual-explainable observations still discriminate:
70	  1. **NIF-B (third-party application)** fires P4-HD (O3) and can establish N-FORCE for P1, P5, P7 and P8. It is behaviour, and both hypotheses explain it (N1). HUMAN-DECISIONS' principle that "a work event alone cannot establish a norm change" applies equally to a non-executor's act.
71	  2. **The absence of a permitting act** is used to establish non-permission (ACT-CONTRA, the graded fallback, the C1 default, O5). This observation is compatible with "H-D P1 holds and H-B conformance fails" and with "H-D P1 fails and H-B conformance holds" (N2). G-D1 does not catch it, because G-D1 is limited to the status rule.
72	- **Is the fallback independent?** No. The graded fallback (the maker's records) is not an independent observable. TASK says "state what additional independent observable … is required, or declare the prediction NON-DISCRIMINATING without it". For P2, P5-HB and P7, the spec takes a third route (FIRED-CONDITIONAL on the maker's records), and it offers that route asymmetrically (N3).
73	- **Where only NIF-A counts, the handling is correct:** P1 and P4 need NIF-A or NIF-B, and otherwise are NON-DISCRIMINATING. Once NIF-B is demoted (N1), these become NIF-A-only. Part C cannot deliver NIF-A (SC-1). The honest expectation is therefore that P1, P4 and P5-HD are NON-DISCRIMINATING, and the spec should say so in the ranking.
74	
75	## 3. The six distinctions
76	
77	| Distinction | Kept separate? | Issue |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Norm exists | Yes | — |
80	| Norm in force | **No, partly** | It is established by NIF-B, which is an *act according to a norm* by a third party (distinction 4 → 2). The absence of a permitting *text* (¬exists) is used to infer that no norm is in force, through ACT-CONTRA (distinction 1 → 2, valid only under H-D P1). |
81	| Known to be in force | **Wording** | Defined as "known or claimed", which conflates knowledge with assertion. The rule that it "never establishes N-FORCE" is right for claims, but makes the category non-factive. |
82	| Act according to | Yes, for the executor | For third parties, it is merged into "in force" (N1). |
83	| Act contrary to | **Partly** | It can be established by "no permitting norm", which is derived from "no permitting act" (N2). |
84	| Change without act | Mostly | If both states are established by NIF-B, a "change" is a change in third-party behaviour (N1). |
85	
86	## 4. Smuggling
87	
88	- **H-D is still smuggled in: PARTIAL.** It enters through the act-exclusivity baseline: "no permitting act ⇒ not permitted" in ACT-CONTRA, the fallback, the FR-D9 default and O5 (N2). It also enters through the asymmetric admission of the maker's records against H-B only (N3). G-D1 neutralises the status rule but not this.
89	- **H-B is smuggled in (overcorrection): YES, in P4 and O3.** NIF-B treats practice as force, which is H-B's own ontology used to falsify H-D (N1). "Already governs", written by the sole adopter, is frozen as non-adoption with an unscored sensitivity (N4). Together they let O3 fire P4-HD in a scenario fully consistent with H-D.
90	- **Net effect.** Each hypothesis's falsifier contains a premise drawn from the other hypothesis. The repair is symmetric in form but not in substance.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 5. Rank-0 protocol (Part B): **FAIL, do not execute**
95	
96	**What is right:**
97	- The channel set is explicit and there is no lower bound.
98	- PAT is case-sensitive, with boundaries.
99	- Variant hits go to a separate bucket and are never counted.
100	- The ET-1, ET-2 and MENTION classes have a frozen rule and quoted clauses.
101	- Ancestry-minimal defines "earliest". Git dates are SOURCE_STATED only. Order relative to decision or entry into force is always NOT_IDENTIFIABLE. **M-TIME is respected: no timestamp is used for decision or effectiveness.**
102	- Absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE unless C1–C4 are shown, and CAPTURE_INVALID is kept apart from absence. **Absence is handled correctly.**
103	- The worker/reviewer split, the blind reclassification and the DISPUTED handling are good.
104	
105	**Blocking defects:**
106	
107	| # | Class | Defect | Failure scenario |
108	|---|---|---|---|
109	| **R0-1** | coding | **Run B cannot run.** W4 runs `rank0-wp4c1.sh` in `git clone --mirror`, which is a **bare** repository. S0 calls `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and since git 2.25 this dies ("this operation must be run in a work tree") outside a work tree. The prerequisite is git ≥ 2.31. Under `set -euo pipefail` the script aborts at `00_env.txt`. (Confidence: high.) | W5 gives CAPTURE_ERROR on every run. PRIMARY results "come from Run B", so no valid result can exist, and the reviewer's R2 rerun fails the same way. The protocol forbids ad-hoc fixes, so it cannot produce an output. |
110	| **R0-2** | evidence scope; coding | **C2 conflicts with the fetch refspec.** `rank0-fetch.sh` fetches with the default refspecs (heads and tags). `ls-remote --refs` also lists `refs/pull/*/{head,merge}` (GitHub) and `refs/merge-requests/*/head` (GitLab), whose objects are usually not fetched. Examples: synthetic PR merge commits, squash-merged MR heads, fork PR heads. (Confidence: high for GitHub PR merge refs.) | `08_remote_objects.txt` contains MISSING, so C2 fails and the capture is CAPTURE_INVALID on any hosted repository with PRs or MRs. Conversely, unmerged or squashed MR work on WP-4C-1, which is prime execution evidence, is never searched, although B.1 claims "all refs". `refs/notes` is claimed but is not fetched by default either. |
111	
112	**Non-blocking but must be fixed in r2:**
113	
114	| # | Class | Defect |
115	|---|---|---|
116	| R0-3 | coding | The path-name pass (`15_paths.txt`) is **not included in `90_hitset.txt`**. ET-2 clause 3 ("a NON_DOC path name matches PAT") therefore never reaches `93_details`, ancestry, or `rank0-order.sh`. If such hashes are put into `$ET`, they have no ancestry rows and appear ancestry-minimal when they are not. |
117	| R0-4 | coding | Under `LC_ALL=C`, VAR's `[^0-9a-z]{0,2}` counts **bytes**. U+2010, U+2011 and U+2013 are 3 bytes in UTF-8, so "WP‑4C‑1" with non-ASCII hyphens is **not** matched, contrary to B.2. The variant bucket is under-inclusive exactly where the spec says it is covered. |
118	| R0-5 | coding (over-inclusion) | ET-1 fires on any subject or trailer mention plus one NON_DOC change. Examples: "WP-4B: unblock WP-4C-1 after R-89" together with WP-4B code (MIXED is recorded but has no effect on the class); a register, queue or work-plan commit in `register.yaml`, `queue.json` or `workplan.yml` (none of these match DOC_GOV unless their directory name does). ET-2 fires on a `TODO(WP-4C-1)` comment. In each case a plan or ruling becomes t_w, the premise of P7-HB. Fix: MIXED demotes ET-1 to ET-2 unless WP-4C-1 is the *first* WP id; add `ya?ml|json|csv|toml` files with governance-stem names to DOC_GOV; comment-only added lines count as MENTION. |
119	| R0-6 | coding | Merge rule: "NON_DOC changes not present in any other hit commit" gives no criterion for identity (path? blob? hunk?). It is not operational. |
120	| R0-7 | coding; reproducibility | CLOCK_ANOMALY is defined but **computed by no script**. The global git config (`~/.gitconfig`) is not isolated: only `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` is set, not `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. The "byte-identical with same git version" claim is false, because `00_env.txt` (toplevel path) and `04_remotes.txt` (bundle path) are machine-specific. Classification W7 is manual, which is acceptable only because of R3's blind double coding. |
121	| R0-8 | evidence scope (under-inclusion) | Ref **names** (for example `feature/WP-4C-1`) are captured in `01_refs.tsv` but not matched against PAT. Work on an unmerged branch named for the package, but without the token in its messages, is invisible, although it is the cheapest identifier channel. |
122	| R0-9 | coding (minor) | There is a race between `fetch` and `ls-remote`. The awk path extraction uses `$2`, which truncates paths with spaces, and it maps deleted-file lines to `/dev/null`. |
123	
124	**Target matching:**
125	- **Over-inclusive** through ET-1/ET-2 mentions (R0-5).
126	- **Under-inclusive** through untokened work (disclosed), ref names (R0-8), variant hyphens (R0-4), and unfetched MR/PR refs (R0-2).
127	- The exclusions (WP-4C-10, bare WP-4C, WP-4B) are correct.
128	
129	**"Execution trace" vs "mention":** operational in principle (a path-class rule plus message position), but miscalibrated (R0-5, R0-6).
130	
131	## 6. Scoping protocol (Part C): **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS**
132	
133	**Passes:**
134	- It is **bounded**: a fixed list of 10 channels, one script, a stop rule, and CANDIDATE_NOT_CHECKED for anything else.
135	- It is essentially **existence and metadata only**.
136	- The independence criteria I1–I4 and the completeness criteria K1–K4 are explicit and graded.
137	- NOT_ACCESSIBLE is never recorded as NO, HOST = none gives SERVER_CHANNELS_UNCHECKED, and API reproducibility is correctly marked LIMITED.
138	
139	**Limitations (the result must be read in their light):**
140	
141	| # | Class | Issue |
142	|---|---|---|
143	| **SC-1** | formal reasoning | **NIF_A_CHANNEL_EXISTS is unreachable by construction.** Q5 = YES needs Q2 ∋ NORM_STATE. But Q2 is derived "from channel type, not content", and the only candidate type that could hold NORM_STATE (K-STATUS) is UNKNOWN_CONTENT by rule. I2 (derivation) also needs content, so Q7 = INDEPENDENT is unreachable. The protocol's answer is fixed before it is run. |
144	| **SC-2** | formal reasoning | The Q5 vocabulary {YES, PARTIAL, NO} has **no UNKNOWN**, so unread K-STATUS content is forced to NO. "NO_NIF_A_CHANNEL_IN_CHECKED_SET" then reads as a negative finding. This violates the spec's own rule that "not evidenced" is not "absent". Report it as NIF_A_NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK. |
145	| SC-3 | evidence scope; M-TIME | Paths come only from the **current** default-branch tree (`ls-tree $DEF`). CI, hook or status files that existed during the window and were later deleted are missed. The "ever-existed" comment is inaccurate, and the current configuration does not show the configuration then in force. |
146	| SC-4 | evidence scope | K3 (configuration stability) and Part B's C3 (no force-push or deletion) need audit-log *content*. The script fetches only one `created_at` value. So COMPLETE_SHOWN, and hence ABSENT_IN_COMPLETE_CHANNEL and any "complete DCS", are unreachable with the frozen commands. The spec implies that Part C can supply them. The practical consequence is that every absence-premised falsifier is UNDETERMINED, and the §4 ranking should say so. |
147	| SC-5 | wording (internal inconsistency) | `58_path_history_meta.txt` outputs author **names and emails**, contrary to C.1's "roles, not personal names". |
148	| SC-6 | evidence scope | The completeness window is hard-coded to 2026-08-02..15. This conflicts with FR-D4, under which rank-0 has no lower bound and the P7 window may start before R-72. |
149	| SC-7 | coding | Host detection uses a URL substring: self-hosted GitLab or GHE gives HOST = none (disclosed as UNKNOWN). STATUS_RE is over-broad (`norm` also matches `normalize`), which adds noise but stays bounded. |
150	
151	---
152	
153	## 7. Disagreements
154	
155	1. **With SPEC-r1 D1(3):** "no single observation can be counted for both sides" is false. Third-party application (N1) and the absence of a permitting act (N2) each serve both sides.
156	2. **With SPEC-r1 D2(3):** "the outcome table is exhaustive over the branches" is false (N7).
157	3. **With SPEC-r1 D9(3):** "the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen" is false (N6).
158	4. **With REVIEW-1bb D1 (partly):** I agree with SPEC-r1 that bare citation shows only N-KNOWN. I go further: *application* by a non-executor is equally dual-explainable. Only an independent status record (NIF-A) separates the limbs.
159	5. **With REVIEW-1bb D9 (partly):** the reviewer's recommended default ("NON-CONFORMS by default", "unauthorized unless the proviso is shown met") is itself the source of N2 and N6. That default presupposes H-D's act-exclusivity and converts an absence that is not shown into a falsification. UNDETERMINED (or DISJUNCTIVE) is the defensible default.
160	6. **With SPEC-r1 B.7 and B.8:** the byte-identity claim and the claim that the canonical key is independent of the git version and reproducible are not supported (R0-7). Reproducibility actually rests only on the canonical key, and only once R0-1 is fixed.
161	7. **With SPEC-r1 §4:** the ranking of P4+P7 as HIGH is optimistic. Given SC-1 and SC-4, NIF-A and complete-channel absences are unobtainable with the frozen tools. Once N1 and N2 are fixed, the realistic outcomes for P4 and P7 are NON-DISCRIMINATING, DISJUNCTIVE or UNDETERMINED.
162	
163	## 8. Required before any execution or scoring
164	
165	1. **Part B, r2:**
166	   - Run Run B in a non-bare clone of the bundle, or guard `--show-toplevel`.
167	   - Either fetch `+refs/*:refs/*` or restrict C2 to refs in the fetch refspec, and state that MR/PR refs are searched or out of channel.
168	   - Add `15_paths` hits to the hit set.
169	   - Make VAR multibyte-aware, or list explicit byte sequences.
170	   - Recalibrate ET-1 and ET-2 (MIXED, governance data files, comments).
171	   - Compute CLOCK_ANOMALY; set `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`; match PAT against ref names.
172	2. **Spec:**
173	   - Demote NIF-B (N1).
174	   - Extend G-D1 to act-exclusivity (N2).
175	   - Apply the fallback symmetrically or not at all (N3).
176	   - Score O3 under both AF readings (N4).
177	   - Give FR-D9 a verdict precedence and treat an absence that is not shown as UNDETERMINED (N5, N6).
178	   - Rebuild the outcome table and ungate P4 (N7, N8).
179	   - Extend S1-b to the full history (N9, N10); add the R-91/R-94 item (N11); freeze the P1 rules (N12).
180	3. **Part C:**
181	   - Add UNKNOWN to Q5 and rename the negative overall result (SC-1, SC-2).
182	   - Optionally, in r2, list historical paths and drop names and emails from `58`.

# REVIEW of SPEC-r1 (repair of 1bb, plus rank-0 and scoping protocols)

**Inputs used (only these):** REVIEW-TASK.md, REVIEW-1bb.md, TASK.md, HUMAN-DECISIONS.md, SPEC-r1.md, SPEC-r1.json, CHANGELOG.md. No command was run and nothing was collected.

**Limits of this review.**
- SPEC-1bb, HYPOTHESES, IDENTIFIABILITY, CONFORMANCE-CASE and STATE are not among the permitted inputs. So the `[UNCHANGED]` marks, the CHANGELOG "before" column and the source quotes cannot be checked against their originals. They are taken as given.
- Statements about git behaviour come from knowledge of git, not from running it. Each one gives its confidence.

---

## Verdict: **FAIL**

| Component | Verdict | Execute? |
|---|---|---|
| Part A: corrected spec 1bb-r1 | **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS**. 9 of 14 defects fixed, 5 partial, none left unaddressed. But the D1 repair moves the confound instead of removing it (N1, N2). | Not applicable. It must be amended before any Stage 1 scoring. |
| Part B: rank-0 protocol | **FAIL** | **Must not be executed.** Run B, the reproducible run, aborts as frozen (R0-1). The completeness check C2 fails spuriously on ordinary hosted repositories (R0-2). |
| Part C: scoping protocol | **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS** | It may be run, because it is existence-only, bounded and harmless. Its overall result must be read as "not determinable by existence check", not as "no" (SC-1, SC-2). |

The overall verdict is FAIL because one of the two frozen protocols is not executable as written, and the frozen rules forbid ad-hoc fixes (B.8 W5). Protocol r2 is required for Part B.

The repair of the spec itself is careful and mostly real. The six distinctions are introduced, the NIF matrix is given per prediction, G-D1 exists, and D3, D4, D6, D7, D10, D11, D12 and D14 are properly fixed. But the headline D1 repair relocates the confound instead of removing it:
- **H-B is smuggled into H-D's falsifier.** Third-party *application* (NIF-B) is treated as force (N1).
- **H-D is still smuggled into H-B's falsifiers.** "No permitting act ⇒ not permitted" is used unguarded (N2).

---

## 1. Defects D1–D14

| D | Status | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **PARTIAL** | Real structural work: the six distinctions, NIF tiers, G-D1, the per-prediction NIF matrix, and the DISJUNCTIVE grade. Not sufficient, because NIF-B is itself behaviour that both hypotheses explain (N1). G-D1 covers only H-D's *status* rule, not H-D's *act-exclusivity* rule (N2). The fallback is applied asymmetrically (N3). See §2. |
| **D2** | **PARTIAL** | The two-stage acquisition, the items (a)–(d), the effort restatement and O0 are all real. But the claim that the outcome table is exhaustive is false, and O5 is wrong (N7). O0 wrongly removes P4, which after D1 no longer depends on work (N8). |
| **D3** | FIXED | The "only" claim is deleted. The ranking criterion is explicit and labelled PROPOSAL. |
| **D4** | FIXED | Rank-0 has no lower bound. The P7 start is min(R-72 trace, earliest ET). P4 and P5 start at the earliest trace. Recording times are used only as bounds. (There is a residual evidence-scope gap for waivers recorded before the window start: N10.) |
| **D5** | **PARTIAL** | Sub-fixes (a), (c), (d), (e) and (f) are real. (b), late recording, is not operational: Stage 1 reads the DCS only *within* the window, so a late-recorded act is never seen. The rule also covers only acts that *state* an in-window effect (N9). The (c) classification of "R-89 already governs" is an interpretive choice frozen against H-D (N4). |
| **D6** | FIXED | P2 and P7-HB now test conformance only, and responses are moved to P8 with LATE_RESPONSE. Minor gap: the promised check whether R-91 or R-94 refer to R11 is not an item in Stage 1, and Stage 1 is gated on a WP-4C-1 trace (N11). |
| **D7** | FIXED | Separating observation from attestation resolves both contradictions. |
| **D8** | **PARTIAL** | All named fields are added. The P1 per-clause "satisfaction rule" is deferred to "before Stage 1", so it is not frozen (N12). The review JSON `missing_fields` is not an input, so the rest cannot be checked (this is disclosed). |
| **D9** | **PARTIAL** | The single P ∧ ¬B structure, the default scope and the fallback are all added. But the fallback "not earlier than recording time" is only a lower bound, and it conflicts with M-TIME. As a result, "in force before 16:10" can never be shown, and the verdict rule is not mutually exclusive (N5). The default turns an absence that is not shown ("no unresolved governance blockers") into NON-CONFORMS, which breaks §0.8 (N6). The "unauthorized unless shown" baseline carries H-D (N2). |
| **D10** | FIXED | The UNKNOWN label, readings 1a and 1b, the scoping to W, and dropping the tendency reading are all correct. |
| **D11** | FIXED | The artefact/fallback/grade table is complete for the listed items, and git dates are SOURCE_STATED. |
| **D12** | FIXED | P7-HD is NOT_APPLICABLE to R-89, and elsewhere is merged into P1. The motive clause is removed. |
| **D13** | FIXED (with caveat) | Item 1 is relabelled, item 0 (NIF-A) is added, and the eligibility condition is added. The caveat: FR-D13 still certifies "independently observed" through item (2), NIF-B, so N1 carries over. |
| **D14** | FIXED | The relabels and OPTIONAL marks are all present. The conflict is described as "possibly only apparent". |

### New defects introduced or left visible by the repair

| # | Class | Where | Defect | Consequence / fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **N1** | formal reasoning; independence | §0.4 NIF-B; §0.3 N-FORCE row; O3; FR-D13(2) | **NIF-B is behavioural, so the D1 confound returns one actor further out.** A third party "applying R-89 as binding" while R-89 is not adopted is explained by H-D (the third party acted contrary to the unchanged norm, or erred) and by H-B (practice changed the norm). This is exactly the REVIEW-1bb D1 argument, applied to a non-executor. The spec treats it as N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL], and O3 scores **P4-HD FIRED**. This collapses distinction 4 (the third party's act according to a norm) into distinction 2 (the norm in force). Downgrading only when the application is "expressly voided" makes silence count as force. | Extend G-D1 from "executor behaviour" to "any behaviour". If a force premise rests only on NIF-B, grade it DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, third-party conformance}. Only NIF-A (or NIF-B together with NIF-A) can give FIRED. |
| **N2** | formal reasoning; substantive | §0.3 ACT-CONTRA ("absence of any permitting norm … requires a complete DCS"); graded fallback; FR-D9 default "unauthorized unless P shown"; O5 "baseline of no authorization" | **G-D1 is too narrow.** It catches premises that use H-D's *status* rule (force only via adoption). It does not catch premises that use H-D's *act-exclusivity* clause (P1: norms change only through acts). The inference "no permitting act in a complete DCS ⇒ no permitting norm in force" is valid only if H-D's P1 clause holds. Under H-B reading 1, a permission can arise from work without an act. So P2, C1 and O5 falsify H-B conformance on a premise that presupposes H-D. | Add a G-D1(c) rule: a non-permission premise derived from the absence of a permitting act grades DISJUNCTIVE {H-D P1 clause, H-B conformance}, unless NIF-A shows the state. |
| **N3** | formal reasoning | §1.7 P2, P5-HB and P7 rows vs the P4 row; §0.6 MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION | **Asymmetric evidential standard.** The maker's records are admitted as a graded fallback (FIRED-CONDITIONAL, "maker's records state force accurately") when they cut against H-B. The maker's record that states force ("R-89 already governs") is barred even as a conditional premise when it cuts against H-D. The TASK requires NIF *or* NON-DISCRIMINATING. The fallback is neither, and it is offered to one side only. | Either allow the fallback symmetrically (P4-HD FIRED-CONDITIONAL on MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION) or on neither side. Otherwise declare P2 and P7 NON-DISCRIMINATING or FIRED-CONDITIONAL without NIF, and state that the condition includes H-D P1 (N2). |
| **N4** | source interpretation | §0.6 AF list; D5(4) | "R-89 already governs", written by the **sole adopter**, is frozen as not an adoption, and the sensitivity result is "never scored". Together with N1 this gives a concrete false falsification of H-D: the DA declares R-89 governing, a third party applies it, and O3 fires P4-HD, although under H-D the DA's declaration is plausibly the adoption. | Label the classification PROPOSAL/UNKNOWN. Score O3 only if it holds under **both** classifications. Otherwise grade it FIRED-CONDITIONAL(AF-reading). |
| **N5** | formal reasoning; M-TIME | FR-D9 entry-into-force fallback; §0.5 | "Entry into force not earlier than recording time" is (a) not implied by the inputs: decision and effect can precede recording, which the spec's own late-recording rule concedes. It is also (b) only a *lower* bound. So "text in force before 16:10" can never be shown through the fallback. P is then unshowable and NON-CONFORMS follows by default. At the same moment "entry into force NOT_IDENTIFIABLE relative to 16:10" is true, so NON-CONFORMS and UNDETERMINED both hold, and the verdict is not a function. | Give the verdicts a precedence (UNDETERMINED first). Use the fallback only as an existence bound. Where no upper bound on entry into force exists, P and B are NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, which gives UNDETERMINED. |
| **N6** | formal reasoning; evidence scope | FR-D9 P ("no unresolved governance blockers") | Showing P requires showing an **absence**. By §0.8 that needs a complete channel, which is practically unattainable (SC-4). So failing to show an absence becomes NON-CONFORMS, and an H-B falsifier fires on NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE. This contradicts §0.8, FR-D5(e) and D9's own sufficiency claim ("the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen"). | If the proviso's absence clause is NOT-EVIDENCED, C1 is UNDETERMINED, not NON-CONFORMS. |
| **N7** | formal reasoning | §5 outcome table | **Not exhaustive and not exclusive.** (i) Trace cites R-89, ACC, ¬AD, no NIF: no row. (ii) ¬G (gate not in force): no row. (iii) MENTION_ONLY and CAPTURE_ERROR (B.9 labels) are not mapped. (iv) **O5 lacks ¬ACC.** If WP-4B's acceptance is in force, the R-72 gate is satisfied and the work is authorized, yet O5 scores "P7-HB/P2-type FIRED". (v) The joint firing of O2 and O3, and the precedence of O6 over the other rows, are unstated. | Rebuild the table as a decision procedure over (trace class, ACC, G, WV, AD, F89 source), evaluated in a fixed order. Add ¬ACC to O5. |
| **N8** | formal reasoning; evidence scope | FR-D2; O0; Stage 1 gate | After D1, P4-HD (O3) is "whatever the work was", so it does not need a WP-4C-1 trace. Yet O0 says "P4 … discriminate nothing", and S1-e and S1-f (the only NIF acquisitions for R-89) run only if a trace exists. P4 is dropped for a reason that no longer applies. | Run S1-a, S1-b, S1-e and S1-f for P4 regardless of O0. Only P7 is gated on a trace. |
| **N9** | evidence scope | FR-D5(b); S1-b | The late-recording rule cannot fire: S1-b reads the DCS "over the P7 window" only, so acts recorded after the window are never acquired. Acts decided in W but recorded later *without* stating an effect date are not covered at all. | Extend S1-b to the full DCS history up to capture. Treat any post-window act on the same target as possibly late (NOT_IDENTIFIABLE), whether or not it states a date. |
| **N10** | evidence scope | S1-b; P7 WV | "No waiver in force at t_w⁻" needs waivers recorded *before* the window start, but S1-b is bounded by the window. | Read the waiver history from the root of the record. |
| **N11** | evidence scope | D6 vs §5 | "Stage 1 checks whether R-91 or R-94 refer to R11" appears in no S1 item, and Stage 1 is gated on a WP-4C-1 trace. | Add it as a P8 item, not gated on the trace. |
| **N12** | coding | FR-D8 P1 eligibility | The per-clause satisfaction rule is "written before Stage 1", so it is not frozen now. The eligibility definition also derives H-B's "work condition" from the text of H-D-style conditional acts. | Freeze the rules now, or mark P1 NOT_FROZEN. |
| **N13** | wording | §0.9 grades; §0.3 N-KNOWN; §0.6 vs C.5 | The grade vocabulary omits NON-DISCRIMINATING, LEGITIMATED, VACUOUS, ONE-SIDED and NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED, which are all used. N-KNOWN is defined as "known, **or claimed**", which merges factive knowledge (distinction 3) with assertion. DCS v1 membership includes NORM_STATE in §0.6 and the JSON, but not in the C.5 consequences. | Harmonise. |

---

## 2. D1 assessment

- **Is a NIF specified per prediction?** Yes. §1.7 and `nif_matrix` give each limb a requirement and a "without it" status. This part of TASK is met in form.
- **Does the spec avoid presenting a dual-explainable observation as a discriminator?** Not fully. Two dual-explainable observations still discriminate:
  1. **NIF-B (third-party application)** fires P4-HD (O3) and can establish N-FORCE for P1, P5, P7 and P8. It is behaviour, and both hypotheses explain it (N1). HUMAN-DECISIONS' principle that "a work event alone cannot establish a norm change" applies equally to a non-executor's act.
  2. **The absence of a permitting act** is used to establish non-permission (ACT-CONTRA, the graded fallback, the C1 default, O5). This observation is compatible with "H-D P1 holds and H-B conformance fails" and with "H-D P1 fails and H-B conformance holds" (N2). G-D1 does not catch it, because G-D1 is limited to the status rule.
- **Is the fallback independent?** No. The graded fallback (the maker's records) is not an independent observable. TASK says "state what additional independent observable … is required, or declare the prediction NON-DISCRIMINATING without it". For P2, P5-HB and P7, the spec takes a third route (FIRED-CONDITIONAL on the maker's records), and it offers that route asymmetrically (N3).
- **Where only NIF-A counts, the handling is correct:** P1 and P4 need NIF-A or NIF-B, and otherwise are NON-DISCRIMINATING. Once NIF-B is demoted (N1), these become NIF-A-only. Part C cannot deliver NIF-A (SC-1). The honest expectation is therefore that P1, P4 and P5-HD are NON-DISCRIMINATING, and the spec should say so in the ranking.

## 3. The six distinctions

| Distinction | Kept separate? | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| Norm exists | Yes | — |
| Norm in force | **No, partly** | It is established by NIF-B, which is an *act according to a norm* by a third party (distinction 4 → 2). The absence of a permitting *text* (¬exists) is used to infer that no norm is in force, through ACT-CONTRA (distinction 1 → 2, valid only under H-D P1). |
| Known to be in force | **Wording** | Defined as "known or claimed", which conflates knowledge with assertion. The rule that it "never establishes N-FORCE" is right for claims, but makes the category non-factive. |
| Act according to | Yes, for the executor | For third parties, it is merged into "in force" (N1). |
| Act contrary to | **Partly** | It can be established by "no permitting norm", which is derived from "no permitting act" (N2). |
| Change without act | Mostly | If both states are established by NIF-B, a "change" is a change in third-party behaviour (N1). |

## 4. Smuggling

- **H-D is still smuggled in: PARTIAL.** It enters through the act-exclusivity baseline: "no permitting act ⇒ not permitted" in ACT-CONTRA, the fallback, the FR-D9 default and O5 (N2). It also enters through the asymmetric admission of the maker's records against H-B only (N3). G-D1 neutralises the status rule but not this.
- **H-B is smuggled in (overcorrection): YES, in P4 and O3.** NIF-B treats practice as force, which is H-B's own ontology used to falsify H-D (N1). "Already governs", written by the sole adopter, is frozen as non-adoption with an unscored sensitivity (N4). Together they let O3 fire P4-HD in a scenario fully consistent with H-D.
- **Net effect.** Each hypothesis's falsifier contains a premise drawn from the other hypothesis. The repair is symmetric in form but not in substance.

---

## 5. Rank-0 protocol (Part B): **FAIL, do not execute**

**What is right:**
- The channel set is explicit and there is no lower bound.
- PAT is case-sensitive, with boundaries.
- Variant hits go to a separate bucket and are never counted.
- The ET-1, ET-2 and MENTION classes have a frozen rule and quoted clauses.
- Ancestry-minimal defines "earliest". Git dates are SOURCE_STATED only. Order relative to decision or entry into force is always NOT_IDENTIFIABLE. **M-TIME is respected: no timestamp is used for decision or effectiveness.**
- Absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE unless C1–C4 are shown, and CAPTURE_INVALID is kept apart from absence. **Absence is handled correctly.**
- The worker/reviewer split, the blind reclassification and the DISPUTED handling are good.

**Blocking defects:**

| # | Class | Defect | Failure scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R0-1** | coding | **Run B cannot run.** W4 runs `rank0-wp4c1.sh` in `git clone --mirror`, which is a **bare** repository. S0 calls `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and since git 2.25 this dies ("this operation must be run in a work tree") outside a work tree. The prerequisite is git ≥ 2.31. Under `set -euo pipefail` the script aborts at `00_env.txt`. (Confidence: high.) | W5 gives CAPTURE_ERROR on every run. PRIMARY results "come from Run B", so no valid result can exist, and the reviewer's R2 rerun fails the same way. The protocol forbids ad-hoc fixes, so it cannot produce an output. |
| **R0-2** | evidence scope; coding | **C2 conflicts with the fetch refspec.** `rank0-fetch.sh` fetches with the default refspecs (heads and tags). `ls-remote --refs` also lists `refs/pull/*/{head,merge}` (GitHub) and `refs/merge-requests/*/head` (GitLab), whose objects are usually not fetched. Examples: synthetic PR merge commits, squash-merged MR heads, fork PR heads. (Confidence: high for GitHub PR merge refs.) | `08_remote_objects.txt` contains MISSING, so C2 fails and the capture is CAPTURE_INVALID on any hosted repository with PRs or MRs. Conversely, unmerged or squashed MR work on WP-4C-1, which is prime execution evidence, is never searched, although B.1 claims "all refs". `refs/notes` is claimed but is not fetched by default either. |

**Non-blocking but must be fixed in r2:**

| # | Class | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| R0-3 | coding | The path-name pass (`15_paths.txt`) is **not included in `90_hitset.txt`**. ET-2 clause 3 ("a NON_DOC path name matches PAT") therefore never reaches `93_details`, ancestry, or `rank0-order.sh`. If such hashes are put into `$ET`, they have no ancestry rows and appear ancestry-minimal when they are not. |
| R0-4 | coding | Under `LC_ALL=C`, VAR's `[^0-9a-z]{0,2}` counts **bytes**. U+2010, U+2011 and U+2013 are 3 bytes in UTF-8, so "WP‑4C‑1" with non-ASCII hyphens is **not** matched, contrary to B.2. The variant bucket is under-inclusive exactly where the spec says it is covered. |
| R0-5 | coding (over-inclusion) | ET-1 fires on any subject or trailer mention plus one NON_DOC change. Examples: "WP-4B: unblock WP-4C-1 after R-89" together with WP-4B code (MIXED is recorded but has no effect on the class); a register, queue or work-plan commit in `register.yaml`, `queue.json` or `workplan.yml` (none of these match DOC_GOV unless their directory name does). ET-2 fires on a `TODO(WP-4C-1)` comment. In each case a plan or ruling becomes t_w, the premise of P7-HB. Fix: MIXED demotes ET-1 to ET-2 unless WP-4C-1 is the *first* WP id; add `ya?ml|json|csv|toml` files with governance-stem names to DOC_GOV; comment-only added lines count as MENTION. |
| R0-6 | coding | Merge rule: "NON_DOC changes not present in any other hit commit" gives no criterion for identity (path? blob? hunk?). It is not operational. |
| R0-7 | coding; reproducibility | CLOCK_ANOMALY is defined but **computed by no script**. The global git config (`~/.gitconfig`) is not isolated: only `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` is set, not `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. The "byte-identical with same git version" claim is false, because `00_env.txt` (toplevel path) and `04_remotes.txt` (bundle path) are machine-specific. Classification W7 is manual, which is acceptable only because of R3's blind double coding. |
| R0-8 | evidence scope (under-inclusion) | Ref **names** (for example `feature/WP-4C-1`) are captured in `01_refs.tsv` but not matched against PAT. Work on an unmerged branch named for the package, but without the token in its messages, is invisible, although it is the cheapest identifier channel. |
| R0-9 | coding (minor) | There is a race between `fetch` and `ls-remote`. The awk path extraction uses `$2`, which truncates paths with spaces, and it maps deleted-file lines to `/dev/null`. |

**Target matching:**
- **Over-inclusive** through ET-1/ET-2 mentions (R0-5).
- **Under-inclusive** through untokened work (disclosed), ref names (R0-8), variant hyphens (R0-4), and unfetched MR/PR refs (R0-2).
- The exclusions (WP-4C-10, bare WP-4C, WP-4B) are correct.

**"Execution trace" vs "mention":** operational in principle (a path-class rule plus message position), but miscalibrated (R0-5, R0-6).

## 6. Scoping protocol (Part C): **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS**

**Passes:**
- It is **bounded**: a fixed list of 10 channels, one script, a stop rule, and CANDIDATE_NOT_CHECKED for anything else.
- It is essentially **existence and metadata only**.
- The independence criteria I1–I4 and the completeness criteria K1–K4 are explicit and graded.
- NOT_ACCESSIBLE is never recorded as NO, HOST = none gives SERVER_CHANNELS_UNCHECKED, and API reproducibility is correctly marked LIMITED.

**Limitations (the result must be read in their light):**

| # | Class | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| **SC-1** | formal reasoning | **NIF_A_CHANNEL_EXISTS is unreachable by construction.** Q5 = YES needs Q2 ∋ NORM_STATE. But Q2 is derived "from channel type, not content", and the only candidate type that could hold NORM_STATE (K-STATUS) is UNKNOWN_CONTENT by rule. I2 (derivation) also needs content, so Q7 = INDEPENDENT is unreachable. The protocol's answer is fixed before it is run. |
| **SC-2** | formal reasoning | The Q5 vocabulary {YES, PARTIAL, NO} has **no UNKNOWN**, so unread K-STATUS content is forced to NO. "NO_NIF_A_CHANNEL_IN_CHECKED_SET" then reads as a negative finding. This violates the spec's own rule that "not evidenced" is not "absent". Report it as NIF_A_NOT_DETERMINABLE_BY_EXISTENCE_CHECK. |
| SC-3 | evidence scope; M-TIME | Paths come only from the **current** default-branch tree (`ls-tree $DEF`). CI, hook or status files that existed during the window and were later deleted are missed. The "ever-existed" comment is inaccurate, and the current configuration does not show the configuration then in force. |
| SC-4 | evidence scope | K3 (configuration stability) and Part B's C3 (no force-push or deletion) need audit-log *content*. The script fetches only one `created_at` value. So COMPLETE_SHOWN, and hence ABSENT_IN_COMPLETE_CHANNEL and any "complete DCS", are unreachable with the frozen commands. The spec implies that Part C can supply them. The practical consequence is that every absence-premised falsifier is UNDETERMINED, and the §4 ranking should say so. |
| SC-5 | wording (internal inconsistency) | `58_path_history_meta.txt` outputs author **names and emails**, contrary to C.1's "roles, not personal names". |
| SC-6 | evidence scope | The completeness window is hard-coded to 2026-08-02..15. This conflicts with FR-D4, under which rank-0 has no lower bound and the P7 window may start before R-72. |
| SC-7 | coding | Host detection uses a URL substring: self-hosted GitLab or GHE gives HOST = none (disclosed as UNKNOWN). STATUS_RE is over-broad (`norm` also matches `normalize`), which adds noise but stays bounded. |

---

## 7. Disagreements

1. **With SPEC-r1 D1(3):** "no single observation can be counted for both sides" is false. Third-party application (N1) and the absence of a permitting act (N2) each serve both sides.
2. **With SPEC-r1 D2(3):** "the outcome table is exhaustive over the branches" is false (N7).
3. **With SPEC-r1 D9(3):** "the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen" is false (N6).
4. **With REVIEW-1bb D1 (partly):** I agree with SPEC-r1 that bare citation shows only N-KNOWN. I go further: *application* by a non-executor is equally dual-explainable. Only an independent status record (NIF-A) separates the limbs.
5. **With REVIEW-1bb D9 (partly):** the reviewer's recommended default ("NON-CONFORMS by default", "unauthorized unless the proviso is shown met") is itself the source of N2 and N6. That default presupposes H-D's act-exclusivity and converts an absence that is not shown into a falsification. UNDETERMINED (or DISJUNCTIVE) is the defensible default.
6. **With SPEC-r1 B.7 and B.8:** the byte-identity claim and the claim that the canonical key is independent of the git version and reproducible are not supported (R0-7). Reproducibility actually rests only on the canonical key, and only once R0-1 is fixed.
7. **With SPEC-r1 §4:** the ranking of P4+P7 as HIGH is optimistic. Given SC-1 and SC-4, NIF-A and complete-channel absences are unobtainable with the frozen tools. Once N1 and N2 are fixed, the realistic outcomes for P4 and P7 are NON-DISCRIMINATING, DISJUNCTIVE or UNDETERMINED.

## 8. Required before any execution or scoring

1. **Part B, r2:**
   - Run Run B in a non-bare clone of the bundle, or guard `--show-toplevel`.
   - Either fetch `+refs/*:refs/*` or restrict C2 to refs in the fetch refspec, and state that MR/PR refs are searched or out of channel.
   - Add `15_paths` hits to the hit set.
   - Make VAR multibyte-aware, or list explicit byte sequences.
   - Recalibrate ET-1 and ET-2 (MIXED, governance data files, comments).
   - Compute CLOCK_ANOMALY; set `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`; match PAT against ref names.
2. **Spec:**
   - Demote NIF-B (N1).
   - Extend G-D1 to act-exclusivity (N2).
   - Apply the fallback symmetrically or not at all (N3).
   - Score O3 under both AF readings (N4).
   - Give FR-D9 a verdict precedence and treat an absence that is not shown as UNDETERMINED (N5, N6).
   - Rebuild the outcome table and ungate P4 (N7, N8).
   - Extend S1-b to the full history (N9, N10); add the R-91/R-94 item (N11); freeze the P1 rules (N12).
3. **Part C:**
   - Add UNKNOWN to Q5 and rename the negative overall result (SC-1, SC-2).
   - Optionally, in r2, list historical paths and drop names and emails from `58`.

# Research state (facts to design against; established by reviewed prior tasks)
- The corpus is a **register of rulings** (norm-making acts and their normative content), plus a few session logs and one git commit.
- **Act records are almost all performed acts** (23 performed vs 1 refused under the current coding). So no act-level contrasts exist.
- **Norm records:** permissions to start work change per target across successive rulings.
- **Status mediation:** a Chief-prepared ruling gains force when the Decision Authority adopts it. There are 2 episodes, both **self-reported by the rulings themselves**.
- **One execution record** (a commit, "WP-4B RED") appears **not to conform** to the norm then in force. Moderate confidence, contested reading.
- The register text mentions further execution reports (e.g. "Executed at IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md:58") that are **not yet coded**.
- **Recording time ≠ decision time ≠ entry into force.** Prepared rulings are written before they are adopted.

575	### §0.9 M-TIME: order labels, late recording, grades [NEW D4, D5, D11]
576	- **Order labels**, for any claimed order between two events:
577	  - **RECORDING_ORDER**: an order of recording established by the recording system's structure. Example: git ancestry, where a child commit embeds its parent's hash, so the parent existed first.
578	  - **SOURCE_STATED_ORDER**: an order stated by a source, or by metadata set by an actor. Examples: git author and committer dates, dates written in texts, the textual order of citations.
579	  - **INFERRED_ORDER**: an order derived by combining two or more premises of different kinds, for example ancestry plus a stated date.
580	  - **NOT_IDENTIFIABLE**: none of the above holds, or the premises contradict each other (for example, a clock anomaly against ancestry).
581	- **None of these labels establishes a decision time or entry into force.** An order relative to entry into force needs N-FORCE evidence (§0.3).
582	- **Late recording** **[D5(b)]**. An act whose recording time is after window W, but whose text states an effect inside W, makes both "no act in W" and "act in force in W" **NOT_IDENTIFIABLE** for that target.
583	- **Falsifier grades:**
584	  - **FIRED**: all premises are established by NIF-A or NIF-B, with AUTH_ID, and absences are shown complete.
585	  - **FIRED-CONDITIONAL(conditions)**: fires given listed weaker premises (SOURCE_STATED times, ACTOR_SET_ID, the maker's records).
586	  - **DISJUNCTIVE{…}**: by G-D1.
587	  - **NOT-FIRED**: premises established, and the falsifier condition is false.
588	  - **UNDETERMINED**: some premise is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, or an absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE.
589	  - **NOT_APPLICABLE**: the falsifier's precondition cannot hold in the episode.

593	- they concern different targets or work packages;
594	- they are governed by different acts;
595	- different adoption acts bring those acts into force;

### §0.9 M-TIME: order labels, late recording, grades [NEW D4, D5, D11]
- **Order labels**, for any claimed order between two events:
  - **RECORDING_ORDER**: an order of recording established by the recording system's structure. Example: git ancestry, where a child commit embeds its parent's hash, so the parent existed first.
  - **SOURCE_STATED_ORDER**: an order stated by a source, or by metadata set by an actor. Examples: git author and committer dates, dates written in texts, the textual order of citations.
  - **INFERRED_ORDER**: an order derived by combining two or more premises of different kinds, for example ancestry plus a stated date.
  - **NOT_IDENTIFIABLE**: none of the above holds, or the premises contradict each other (for example, a clock anomaly against ancestry).
- **None of these labels establishes a decision time or entry into force.** An order relative to entry into force needs N-FORCE evidence (§0.3).
- **Late recording** **[D5(b)]**. An act whose recording time is after window W, but whose text states an effect inside W, makes both "no act in W" and "act in force in W" **NOT_IDENTIFIABLE** for that target.
- **Falsifier grades:**
  - **FIRED**: all premises are established by NIF-A or NIF-B, with AUTH_ID, and absences are shown complete.
  - **FIRED-CONDITIONAL(conditions)**: fires given listed weaker premises (SOURCE_STATED times, ACTOR_SET_ID, the maker's records).
  - **DISJUNCTIVE{…}**: by G-D1.
  - **NOT-FIRED**: premises established, and the falsifier condition is false.
  - **UNDETERMINED**: some premise is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, or an absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE.
  - **NOT_APPLICABLE**: the falsifier's precondition cannot hold in the episode.

### §0.10 Independence of episodes [UNCHANGED]
Two episodes are independent if all of these hold:
- they concern different targets or work packages;
- they are governed by different acts;
- different adoption acts bring those acts into force;
- their execution artefacts are separate (not successive commits of one batch or session);
- their attestation sources are not copies of each other.

### §0.11 Artefact existence and fallbacks [NEW D11]

| Field or assumption in 1bb | Preferred artefact (if it exists) | Fallback | Grade of fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| CI start time | CI run record from the CI system | Commit dates plus ancestry | SOURCE_STATED / RECORDING_ORDER |
| Server push time | Hosting server audit or event record | None in git | UNDETERMINED |
| "Adopted" R-86 | AF-1/2/3 entry for R-86 with recording time | R-86 text as quoted (SOURCE FACT: names the DA as sole adopter) | FIRED-CONDITIONAL premise |
| "Adopted" R-90 | R-90 text plus status | **UNKNOWN** (withdrawal context) | P5 is NON-DISCRIMINATING while unresolved |
| Adoption records for R-77, R-79, R-80 | AF-1/2/3 | Recording time of the ruling as "not earlier than" | SOURCE_STATED unless versioned |
| DA session logs | Session logs with system time | S0804 and S0815 as known session logs | SOURCE_STATED |
| IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md under version control | Revision introducing line 58 | Line-58 text as a report | Execution for P5 becomes a report only (MENTION/REPORT); P5 is UNDETERMINED |
| Register kept as a git file | Write history of the register file | Register text with its stated dates | No write history; "no act" absences are NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE |
| R11 time "16:10" | CI or server record | Git author and committer dates | SOURCE_STATED |

## §1. Specifications

### P1: norm changes occur only through norm-making acts [CHANGED D1, D5, D8, D10]

  - **H-B, reading 1:** work changes a norm with no act.
  - **UNKNOWN:** which reading of H-B is intended. Under reading 2 (acts triggered by work), P1 cannot discriminate even in principle.
- **Claim [UNCHANGED]:** every change in a target's deontic state is preceded by an act in the DCS whose content produces that state. Conditional content counts if the act stated the condition in advance.
- **Fields.**
  - `target` [UNCHANGED]
  - `norm_state_before` **[CHANGED D1]**: N-FORCE at t1 by NIF-A or NIF-B. The last execution or refusal is recorded as ACT only.
